raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Allow the Python frontend to accept managed global DP ranks in `X-data-parallel-rank` with hybrid or external load balancing, while preserving existing local-index callers. Fixes #64801.

## Claims

- Normalize an accepted global rank to the local engine index expected by the core client.
- Preserve local-index precedence when ranges overlap, unpinned requests, and internal-LB behavior. Reject ranks outside both valid ranges.
- Document the frontend-specific header semantics and cover the normalization and real HTTP request paths.

## Validation

Base: `7b77ed581d92fa14e34ab43344837bb1ca1b4257`; the production source is unchanged for the before-fix runs, with the new regression tests applied. The test code, Python/PyTorch versions and model configuration are unchanged across comparisons; both HTTP runs use the aligned CUDA 13.0 environment (the initial CPU input test preceded that compiler alignment).

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 13 real InputProcessor cases | 3 failed, 10 passed; global aliases rejected | 13 passed |
| Real external-LB HTTP regression, 1 API process | HTTP 400 for global rank 1 (`out of range [0, 1)`) | Passed |
| Same HTTP regression across 1 API, 4 API and EP-enabled fixtures | Baseline run limited to 1 API | 3 passed |
| Applicable pre-commit hooks over all four changed files | — | 16 passed |

```bash
# Python 3.12 environment, installed with uv and an editable precompiled vLLM build.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/distributed/test_external_lb_dp.py -v -s -k dp_rank_input_normalization
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,0 DP_SIZE=2 TP_SIZE=1 MODEL_NAME=/path/to/granite-3.0-1b-a400m-base \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/distributed/test_external_lb_dp.py -v -s -k external_lb_global_rank_header
# Before-fix HTTP run uses this narrower filter instead: -k 'external_lb_global_rank_header and api-1-standard'
```

<details>
<summary>Actual regression output</summary>

```text
base-unit:
E           vllm.exceptions.VLLMValidationError: data_parallel_rank 2 is out of range [0, 1).
E           vllm.exceptions.VLLMValidationError: data_parallel_rank 3 is out of range [0, 2).
E           vllm.exceptions.VLLMValidationError: data_parallel_rank 2 is out of range [0, 2).
================= 3 failed, 10 passed, 20 deselected in 16.32s =================
base-serving:
E               openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - data_parallel_rank 1 is out of range [0, 1).
================= 1 failed, 32 deselected in 125.79s (0:02:05) =================
fixed-unit:
====================== 13 passed, 20 deselected in 4.91s =======================
fixed-serving-all:
================= 3 passed, 30 deselected in 145.15s (0:02:25) =================
```

</details>

Hardware/model: two NVIDIA A100 80GB PCIe GPUs, DP=2/TP=1, BF16, eager execution, max model length 2048; `ibm-granite/granite-3.0-1b-a400m-base` at `d91cbed802d85eb1b32374623331f6ab2b37403a`. Torch `2.14.0+cu130`, CUDA toolkit 13.0 and a task-local driver compatibility library. The editable build uses the official precompiled artifact at `87cb835db2bbbaa03e3faa6ae588ba92dce1eea4`; its diff to the tested source contains no native/build changes.

The HTTP regression compares unpinned and pinned greedy completions using `check_logprobs_close`, checks nonempty output, and verifies an unmanaged rank returns HTTP 400. The existing `distributed-dp-tests-2-gpus` Buildkite step selects this file and covers the changed engine path. Hybrid/overlap cases are covered through real InputProcessor constructors; multi-node, four-GPU hybrid and Rust serving were not run. No throughput or broad model-quality claim.

## Details

The frontend previously checked only `[0, data_parallel_size_local)`, while routers, metrics and the Rust frontend use global ranks. `InputProcessor` now falls back to the endpoint's managed global range only after the local range fails, subtracting `data_parallel_index` before dispatch. This leaves the core client's local-index contract unchanged and adds no scheduler or GPU-kernel changes.

Overlap is intentionally backward compatible: with start=1/local_size=2, header `1` still means local index 1 (global rank 2). This does not claim identical Python/Rust semantics in overlapping ranges.

Local-index compatibility is not strict global-rank ownership validation: a request sent to the wrong endpoint is still accepted if its header is a valid local index there. With uneven per-node sizes, overlapping local/global ranges can also make a router-intended global rank select a different local engine. The serving guide now explicitly warns about both limitations, as discussed in [the issue feedback](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64801#issuecomment-6575504490).

Duplicate-work checks covered issue comments, assignees, linked PRs, issue-number and rank-header searches, and current main. No equivalent open Python alias implementation was found. Router PR llm-d/llm-d-router#3761, Rust multi-port PR #64426 and device-visibility PR #41164 address different layers.

AI assistance was used for source investigation, implementation, regression tests, documentation and validation. I personally reviewed the complete diff and PR description, understand the validation scope, and ran the verification script: 13 input-processing cases passed (5.32s), followed by the real two-GPU HTTP regression (1 passed, 47.62s). The tested file hashes match this submitted tree.

files.patch: @@ -141,3 +141,29 @@ The coordinator process also runs in this scenario, co-located with the DP rank In the above diagram, each of the dotted boxes corresponds to a separate launch of `vllm serve` - these could be separate Kubernetes pods, for example. + +## Routing requests with `X-data-parallel-rank` + +The `X-data-parallel-rank` HTTP header pins a request to a particular data-parallel engine. Without the header, the frontend uses its configured load balancing. + +With hybrid or external load balancing, the Python API server accepts both: + +- A local engine index in `[0, data_parallel_size_local)`. +- A global DP rank managed by that endpoint, starting at `--data-parallel-start-rank` for hybrid load balancing or `--data-parallel-rank` for external load balancing. + +For example, a hybrid endpoint managing global ranks `2` and `3` accepts header `0` or `2` for global rank `2`, and header `1` or `3` for global rank `3`. An external endpoint managing only global rank `3` accepts header `0` or `3`. + +Local indices take precedence when the ranges overlap, preserving existing callers. For an endpoint managing global ranks `1` and `2`, header `1` still selects local index `1` (global rank `2`). Values outside both ranges are rejected; this header cannot route a request to an engine outside the endpoint's managed group. + +!!! warning "Local-index compatibility is not strict global-rank validation" + + A request sent to the wrong endpoint is still accepted if its header is a + valid local index there. For example, an endpoint managing global rank `2` + accepts header `0`, even if the router intended global rank `0`. + + Uneven per-node DP sizes can also produce overlapping local and global + ranges. In that case, a router intending a managed global rank may select a + different engine because local indices take precedence. Routers must account + for this interpretation and validate their endpoint/rank mapping. + +With internal load balancing, the Python API server continues to accept ranks in `[0, data_parallel_size)`. The Rust frontend interprets the header as a global rank.
